A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedOT research. Their main texts, appendices, tables, figures, and equations are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original five-dataset federated-learning experiments, component ablations, and communication-frequency and client-scaling studies in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results, gradient-conflict measurements, ablations, scalability experiments, and runtime comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: Both versions use a frozen black-box image encoder, a shared linear classifier, client-local orthogonal transformations parameterized through the Cayley transform, cross-entropy optimization, and server averaging. Block-diagonal transformations and random classifier initialization already exist in v1. The new comparison architectures do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate FEMNIST, PACS, Office-Home, VLCS, and TerraIncognita, retaining the same cross-domain classification coverage and FEMNIST cross-device setting. Increasing participant counts extends an existing experiment rather than introducing a new dataset, task, or population.

E2.justification: V3 adds nonlinear FedAdapter comparisons and introduces PromptFL into the cross-device study. FedOT(-o), renamed FedLT, expands from the three-dataset condition-number comparison to the full benchmark suite, and local-only comparisons broaden. FedAVG is simply renamed FedOT(All Global). Detailed benchmark tables remove the random-initialization variant, although the separate initialization ablation remains.

E3.justification: V3 extends client-scaling evaluation to 1–75 participants; v1 describes 2–15 in its text and plots through 20 in Figure 5. It introduces round-averaged pseudo-gradient cosine similarity as an evaluation measure. Reported block settings change from 4 to 1 for VLCS and 16 to 4 for TerraIncognita. The base data splits and generalization, personalization, and comprehensive metrics remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct gradient-conflict analysis comparing orthogonal, unconstrained linear, and nonlinear adaptation (Table 2), expands the condition-number analysis from three datasets to five, and adds computational analysis. The existing scalability study is substantially extended. Initialization, degrees-of-freedom, global/local-component, and communication-frequency ablations already appear in v1.

E5.justification: V1 supplies benchmark point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts. V3 reports means and standard deviations across three named seeds (50, 77, 98) throughout the main and detailed benchmark tables, and specifies three seeds and 12 runs per dataset for gradient-conflict analysis. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, without establishing v1's original run count. No formal significance test is supplied.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation values change extensively. For example, Table 1 reports FEMNIST FedOT generalization as 94.89% in v1 versus 94.23 ± 0.84% in v3; these are revised reporting summaries, not an established same-setting decline. V3 adds gradient-similarity, runtime, and scalability results, including 71.18% for FedOT versus 65.30% for PromptFL at 75 clients. Some revised summaries conflict with appendix entries.

T1.justification: The principal gradient-difference bound remains, but v1 Appendix E.3's prompt-learning extension, including Jacobian and Lipschitz-based reasoning, is removed. V3 corrects the false assertion that orthogonal-matrix eigenvalues must be ±1, replacing it with unit-modulus eigenvalues and a singular-value argument for condition number 1 (Appendix C.2). Separate degrees-of-freedom derivations are also omitted.

C1.justification: V3 narrows the novelty statement from demonstrating orthogonal transformations' effectiveness in FL generally to theoretical and empirical validation specifically in black-box FL. Efficiency and large-scale scalability become explicit headline claims. The central contributions concerning generalization, personalization, representation preservation, and external adaptation remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations concerning poor transfer of conventional personalized-FL methods to foundation models and efficiency from avoiding encoder backpropagation, including a backbone-independent computation claim. It removes the lower-dimensional projection and block-size-selection caveats and adds possible LLM/token-embedding applications. The central interpretation connecting orthogonality, feature preservation, and generalization remains.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies the scalability study's minimum 100 images per client and five test-client IDs, and supplies runtime and parameter-count information. However, it removes v1's exact initialization prompts, optimizer momentum, special random-initialization learning rates, block-search procedure, detailed CoCoOp configuration explanations, and dataset-level training-time ranges. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation, without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: V3 substantially contracts the cited domain-adaptation, foundation-model, and personalized-FL literature, including removing BlackFed and the explicit black-box FL versus black-box foundation-FL taxonomy. Positioning shifts toward incompatibility of white-box adaptation with proprietary models and contrasts FedOT's gradient-based feature adaptation with ZooPFL's query-intensive optimization. These changes exceed bibliographic renumbering or venue updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and results discussion are extensively rewritten around black-box access and dual privacy. Scalability and efficiency receive dedicated subsections, and the supplement is reorganized with shortened background and implementation sections. The title, affiliation notes, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main layout and substantially restructures Table 1 and the detailed appendix tables. It adds gradient-conflict, scalability, and runtime tables, removes the learning-framework comparison table, and moves the communication plot into the main text. Figure 5 changes from per-client improvement curves to absolute-accuracy comparisons among methods.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful uncertainty reporting, mechanism controls, scalability comparisons, and a corrected eigenvalue argument. However, reproducibility details are lost and revised results introduce unresolved contradictions: Office-Home FedAKT(C) personalization is 73.49% in main Table 1, while Appendix Tables 13–14 average approximately 55.34%; the corresponding v1 tables agree at 27.24%. V3 also infers statistical significance from low standard deviations without a test. These issues leave the reliability of the expanded evidence, and therefore the net quality improvement, uncertain.
